q: Do I need a paid database like ecoinvent to calculate a product carbon footprint for an export buyer?
title: Do I need ecoinvent for a product footprint?
short: Not always. If your buyer's request does not name a database, you can build a credible footprint from your own energy and fuel data, supplier figures and free published factors. A paid database like ecoinvent helps when many materials have no free factor, or when the buyer asks for it.
audience: Indian exporters asked for a PCF for the first time

p: ISO 14067 and the GHG Protocol Product Standard ask for site-specific data for processes you control and for inputs that drive most of the result. Secondary data is allowed for the rest, as long as you state its source, year and geography and judge its quality. Neither standard names a database. The PACT Methodology adds that buyers should see how much of the footprint rests on primary data.

sections.h: What you can do with free data
ul: Your own electricity and fuel: kWh x the CEA grid factor, litres or kg x IPCC 2006 defaults.
Main materials: a supplier's own footprint or EPD, which beats any database average.
Free industry figures where they exist, such as worldsteel's published CO2 intensity for steel, labelled as a global average.
Freight: tonne-km x a published mode factor.

sections.h: When a paid database earns its cost
ul: Your bill of materials has many chemicals, polymers or components with no supplier figure and no free factor.
The buyer names ecoinvent or the EU Environmental Footprint datasets, so results compare across its suppliers.
You need a full life cycle model, not only a carbon number.

sections.h: Check the licence before you share
p: Licensed databases restrict how values can be passed on. Send your buyer the result and the dataset names, not tables of licensed factors, unless the licence allows it. Read the publisher's current terms; they change.

List your inputs by weight and cost. If the top few materials and your energy make up most of the footprint and you can get factors for them, start without a paid database. If many large inputs have no factor, or the buyer specifies one, budget for the licence.
